title: MJF Shaped AEW Redemption Main Event as Backstage Creative Force
excerpt: Despite being sidelined with injuries, former AEW World Champion MJF reportedly pushed for the Kevin Knight vs Kenny Omega title match headlining Sunday's pay-per-view in Montreal.
body:
• Fightful Select reports MJF was a "driving creative force" behind the AEW World Championship match between Kenny Omega and Kevin Knight at Redemption
  • The former champion advocated for the TNT Champion to face Omega and supported Knight's heel turn into the Don Callis Family
  • AEW president Tony Khan credited MJF for fighting through injuries in 2026 and confirmed he is expected back when healthy

Maxwell Jacob Friedman lost the AEW World Championship to Kenny Omega at Dynamite: Beach Break on July 8 and has been off television since. But according to a report from Fightful Select, the 30-year-old former champion has remained deeply involved in AEW's creative direction — specifically as the architect behind Sunday's Redemption main event.

The report states MJF was a "driving creative force" behind the World Championship match between reigning TNT Champion Kevin Knight and Omega. Friedman wanted whoever held the TNT title to challenge Omega for the top belt, and while he did not specifically name Knight, he supported the matchup once it materialized. He also reportedly backed Knight's heel turn and his alignment with the Don Callis Family, a storyline shift that began at Double or Nothing 2026.

Knight's Rapid Ascent Through AEW

Kevin Knight, known as "The Jet," signed with AEW in the spring of 2025 and has risen through the ranks at a pace few expected. He captured the TNT Championship earlier this year and has already challenged both MJF and Darby Allin for the World Championship in 2026, falling short both times.

https://x.com/Fightful/status/2080080452652876208

According to Fightful Select, AEW officials are "very high on Knight and what he has produced in the ring this year." The 2026 Redemption pay-per-view, scheduled for July 26 at Montreal's Bell Centre, marks Knight's first-ever PPV main event — and his third shot at the World Championship.

"I am very confident that Knight can be one of the top stars."

— Tony Khan, AEW President, during July 23 media call

Knight earned the title opportunity on the July 15 episode of Dynamite, calling his shot after an in-ring confrontation between Omega and Will Ospreay. He was previously promised a title opportunity by MJF himself for participating on his team during the 12-man cage match at Forbidden Door. The match against Omega will also be the first time the two have faced each other one-on-one, despite having teamed together twice.

MJF's Expanding Role Behind the Scenes

Friedman's creative involvement signals a growing backstage role for one of AEW's biggest homegrown stars. During a media call on Thursday, AEW president Tony Khan addressed MJF's absence from the Redemption card, noting that the former champion had endured some "very hard-hitting matches" in 2026.

"MJF was a fighting champion in 2026, which was very different compared to his previous reigns," Khan said, according to Pro Wrestling Dot Net. "He isn't a nice guy or a good person, but he's a great wrestler, and they love to have him when he's healthy and fit to compete."

Khan gave Friedman credit for fighting through injuries throughout the year. When asked by reporter Jon Alba whether the original plan was for MJF to defend at Redemption, Khan deflected, saying it was a "very fair question," but that he needed to maintain "some sleight of hand."

A Stacked Card in Montreal

Beyond the Omega-Knight main event, AEW Redemption features a loaded card at the Bell Centre — the promotion's first PPV in Montreal. Thekla defends the AEW Women's World Championship against a returning Willow Nightingale. Chris Jericho revives his "Painmaker" persona for a No Holds Barred rematch against Tommaso Ciampa. Kyle Fletcher puts the International Championship on the line against Bandido, and Cage and Cope defend the Tag Team titles against the Death Riders.

The event also features Jon Moxley and Will Ospreay teaming against The Young Bucks, a TBS Championship match between Hikaru Shida and Maya World, and a six-way ladder match to determine the next International Championship contender.

What to Watch For

All eyes will be on whether Knight can finally capture the World Championship and become "Jet 2 Belts." AEW sources told Fightful that regardless of the Redemption outcome, Knight will continue feuding with "world title-level" talent in the months ahead. He is currently entangled with Darby Allin following their Death's Door Steel Cage Match at Forbidden Door.

As for MJF, his return timeline remains unclear, but Khan's comments suggest Friedman is far from done. His willingness to shape storylines while sidelined — and his reported backing of Knight's push — points to a wrestler already thinking beyond his in-ring career, positioning himself for influence that extends well past his next match.
